name: Grilled Romaine Steak Salad with Celery & Dill-Blue Cheese Dressing

cookwares.name: grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 small bunch fresh dill
3 heads romaine lettuce
6 sticks celery

instructions.primary_message: Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half of the dill in a medium bowl. (Reserve remaining dill for serving.)
Peel and mince shallots. Add to the bowl with the dill along with yogurt, mayo, vinegar, Dijon, sugar, and spices. Whisk until smooth.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 shallots
1 cup plain Greek yogurt
3 tbsp mayonnaise
2 tbsp apple cider vinegar
1 tbsp Dijon mustard
1 tbsp brown sugar
¾ tsp garlic powder
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add blue cheese to the bowl and whisk to combine the dressing; set aside.
instructions.secondary_message: 1 ½ (113 g) pkg crumbled blue cheese

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the pan is hot, coat with oil. Working in batches if necessary, add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Meanwhile, trim and quarter romaine heads lengthwise into wedges. Rub cut sides with oil, then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Working in batches if necessary, place romaine quarters, cut-side down, on the pan. Cook, turning halfway through, until charred and leaves begin to wilt, 3-4 minutes. Transfer to another plate.
Meanwhile, trim and medium dice celery.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide romaine between plates, arranging it grilled-side up. Top with steak, dressing, celery, and reserved dill. Enjoy!
